item.title: POINT OF VIEW: Training for high-wage work on waterfront
item.description: THE MARINE TRADES are one of humanity’s oldest activities, and walking through the Northwest School of Wooden Boatbuilding, you can feel the deep roots of the tradition’s history. As the salty sea air mixes with the scent of freshly sanded wood, you can’t help but feel a connection to the rich culture and character inherent in the practice.

item.description: SINCE LAST WEEK we gave out chores you need to do this month, and since many of those chores produce green, leafy debris, and since you eat daily, let me give you a chore — become a “worm farmer!”

item.title: NWAC WOMEN’S TOURNAMENT: Pirates come through in the clutch to hold off Chukars
item.description: PASCO — The Peninsula College women’s basketball team overcame a bad start to its game against Treasure Valley, then held off a late charge from the Chukars with a clutch basket and free throws in the final minute to win its NWAC tournament opener 70-66.
